Fire Emblem Fates Fan Translation Project Has Ceased Development

Archive Link

Fans that were waiting for Team If’s fan translation of Fire Emblem: Fates to be released are in for some bad news, as the team had recently announced that they will be ceasing all future development on the project.

The reason stated was simply that the team was burnt out and did not care to continue it. Any work that they have completed will be retained by the group.

The project originally started before the game was brought over in the west as a means for fans to play an English version of the game before it’s official release, but still continued after it launched with renewed interest in the project after the poor reception of the Fire Emblem: Fates localization.

The project is now left in the air, with the hope that another individual or group continue the project where the original team left off.

Unfortunately this sort of thing has been in the technology industry for a long, long time. For instance, some old card readers could be upgraded simply by opening them up and turning one of the internal belts inside out from its position as sent by the manufacturer. Another example is the 486. The original 486 had a math co-processor, but when they needed to cut costs, they renamed the 486 the 486 DX, then produced the 486 SX, which supposedly had no co-processor, but there was an entire disabled co-processor on at least the first generation of the SX. A similar situation happened with Intel's Core Solo vs. Core Duo several years back, where the Solo was a Duo with a few circuits cut. I'd bet that the Windows Anytime Upgrade is of a similar nature.
